summary: Research complete. The postflight deploy gate cannot live solely in command-gate-out.sh: for the primary meta-task /implement path, status flips to completed inside skill-implementer/SKILL.md's own inline update-task-status.sh call, which runs before gate-out and makes its defensive-correction branch a no-op. Recommended design: an unconditional deploy-freshness backstop inside scripts/update-task-status.sh itself (mirroring the existing --phase-check=warn|refuse precedent), check-only (never itself invoking deploy-headless.sh, to avoid racing parallel per-task postflight calls in multi-task /implement and skill-orchestrate batches), with the actual auto-deploy trigger confined to already-serialized call sites (command-gate-out.sh for single-task, commands/implement.md Step 4 for multi-task batches, and skill-orchestrate's existing Stage MT-3 step 7 for orchestrate -- possibly widened from its current narrow orchestrator-critical-paths.json predicate to full agent-system/extensions/** overlap). The gate must use baseline-relative verify-deploy.sh comparison (new vs pre-existing findings), not raw exit-code checking, because deploy-headless.sh currently exits 3 on every invocation in this repo due to pre-existing unrelated failures -- a naive gate would brick all meta-task completion today. The required regeneration-is-manual-only.md carve-out is specified: a new additive subsection after the existing '## Automated Exception' subsection, naming the new call site(s), following the same not-a-side-effect/not-silent/bounded three-part justification shape, never editing the existing sanctioned-caller text.
